tei:titleStmt.tei:title: אוֹחִיל יוֹם יוֹם
Oḥil Yom Yom (As Every Day I Hope) — a poem to honor the holy city of Tiberias on 7 Elul by David bar Aharon ben Ḥassin

tei:div.tei:head: Oḥil Yom Yom (As Every Day I Hope) — a poem to honor the holy city of Tiberias on 7 Elul by David bar Aharon ben Ḥassin

tei:lg.tei:l: As every day I hope, wondering, my eye always gazing —
Let me go over and see the holy land, Tiberias!
Nice its settlement, so too good is its sight;
the Sea of Galilee its wall, there the city is built.
Let me go over...
Inside it the burials of the righteous-hearted,
who rest in eternal sleep; all lofty people.
Let me go over...
DAre gaze toward the mountain, the grave of our rabbi Yoḥanan
ben Zakkai, lying there, unique in his generation.
Let me go over...
WIth him were five students, righteous and pious,
more precious than gold, their worth he praised.
Let me go over...
Deeming one like a plastered well, never losing a drop,
and his fellow pious, and one sin-fearing.
Let me go over...
Brimming was one with wisdom like a fountain.
Content is she who bore on the birthstool the son of Ḥananya!
Let me go over...
ARranged at the top of the hill is a pillar, the grave of Rabbi ˁAqiva,
with whom were twenty-four thousand students.
Let me go over...
Anyone who sets his mind to see there the faces
of Rabbi Ḥiyya and his schildren Yehuda and Ḥizqiyya is content.
Let me go over...
High atop a high mountain, raised above all,
R. Meir, who is the master of signs and wonders.
Let me go over...
Rabbi Yoḥanan encamped there together with Rav Huna,
and with them Rav Kahana, as well as Rabbi Yirmiya.
Let me go over...
ON it is concealed the grave of Rabbi Moshe bar Maimon,
an interpreter of the true faith, a rabbi over all sages.
Let me go over...
But remember for good the rabbi, our master rabbi,
the tree of life, the general, from the family Abulˁafia.
Let me go over...
ARrayed on his head a holy crown; gentiles seek him out;
from his mouth Torah is saught, from morning until evening.
Let me go over...
ḤASSIN — Mighty one of Yah whom none is like, a holy man of God,
in whose mouth’s exhalations are firestorms, divine flame.
Let me go over...
STRaightening out and renewing the city, its walls and its force,
he sustained its study-hall all his days.
Let me go over...
ONto eternity will his seed live, in his own acquisition.
Let a commoner’s blessing not be taken lightly or ignored!
Let me go over...
Grant that the sound of my cheering hymns, the words and meditations of my mouth,
be before the Cause like pure semolina.
Let me go over...

tei:note.tei:p: Some inverse the clauses beginning with righteous and more precious
The next few verses are based on Avot 2:8.
Some texts read “to be set there, in the sight”

Rabbi Ḥayyim Abulˁafia (1660—1744), whose main work was called the Etz Ḥayyim = Tree of Life. Rabbi Ḥayyim Abulˁafia refounded the Jewish community of Tiberias in 1740, and the next few stanzas of the poem are in his praise.
Some texts read “a crown of the Deity; the people”
Members of the Abulˁafia family live in Tiberias to this day. Some texts read “like item-ownership it should be,” a technical term found throughout the Gemara.
Find Bavli Berakhot 7a — לֹא תְּהֵא בִּרְכַּת הֶדְיוֹט קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ. “The blessing of a commoner should not be light in your eyes.”
